claims: Michigan Wolverines won the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship
1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship was the first national title for Michigan Wolverines
Michigan Wolverines defeated Seton Hall Pirates 80-79 in the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship final
1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship final went to overtime
1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship final was on April 3, 1989
1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship final was at the Kingdome in Seattle
Steve Fisher was interim coach for Michigan in the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship
Glen Rice was tournament MVP of the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship
Michigan secured the win in the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship final on free throws by Rumeal Robinson
Champion of 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship: Michigan Wolverines
Runner-up of 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship: Seton Hall Pirates
Final score of 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship: 80–79 (Overtime)
Most Outstanding Player of 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship: Glen Rice (Michigan)
Glen Rice set a tournament record at the time with 184 points in the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship
Steve Fisher was winning coach of 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship
Steve Fisher took over just before the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship after Bill Frieder was dismissed
Final Four teams of 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship: Michigan, Seton Hall, Illinois, and Duke
Seton Hall led 79-78 with three seconds left in overtime in the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship final
Rumeal Robinson was fouled on a drive with three seconds left in overtime in the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship final
The foul on Rumeal Robinson was dubbed 'The Phantom Foul' by some fans
Rumeal Robinson hit both free throws to win the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship final
Glen Rice scored 31 points in the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship final
Glen Rice averaged 30.7 points over the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship tournament
Michigan’s athletic director was Bo Schembechler
Bo Schembechler forced out head coach Bill Frieder before the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship tournament began
Bill Frieder announced he would leave for Arizona State
Steve Fisher was appointed in Bill Frieder's place as Michigan's coach before the 1989 NCAA Men's Basketball Championship
